entries.answer: An education course trains somebody to teach, and the qualification depends heavily on which level they intend to teach, since primary and secondary requirements differ and special needs adds more. Most programmes combine coursework with supervised classroom practice, because the subject knowledge is rarely the hard part. In the Philippines the path runs through a bachelor's in education with a major in a subject, and the licence to teach follows from it rather than being separate.

entries.answer: A curriculum is the planned content and sequence of what is taught, and it is narrower than a syllabus, which is the assessment that checks it. There is also the hidden curriculum, the habits and expectations a school teaches by its own behaviour, which is what a pupil actually picks up about punctuality and obedience. A curriculum can be national, as in the Philippines' K to 12, or the local version of one that a school chooses within it.

patterns: what is the best teaching method
entries.answer: A teaching method is the plan a teacher follows to get learning out of a class, and the categories go from teacher-led to student-led. Lecture, discussion, demonstration, collaborative and problem-based all produce different classroom shapes, and the useful question is what the lesson is for. If the aim is transmitting information efficiently, lecture wins; if it is applying it, the slower methods win even though they feel less productive from the front.

patterns: how do i choose a course
is it ok to change course
entries.answer: Choosing a course is a decision about which problem you want to spend four years on, and the wrong way to make it is to rank by how the subject sounds. The three things that actually predict whether somebody finishes are whether the work is affordable, whether the daily subject is one they would read about anyway, and whether there is a path out into work. A course with no clear destination can still be a good one, and a fashionable one can still strand you, and the honest answer to which course to take depends on things a written bank cannot see.

entries.answer: A student teacher, or teaching intern, is someone doing supervised teaching as part of their training, and the arrangement is the standard route into the profession. The term practice teaching is the older formal one for the same placement, and both mean working in a real classroom under a mentor teacher who evaluates. The difficulty is nearly always the same: the first lesson is planned in enormous detail, and the last is planned in five minutes because the class will not wait.

patterns: do i need a licence to teach
is a degree enough to teach
entries.answer: A teaching licence is the legal permission to teach a particular level and subject, and it is separate from the degree even where the two are taken together. In the Philippines the licence comes from passing the government exam after a bachelor's in education, and it is what a public school employer actually checks. The reason the distinction matters is that the degree says what was studied while the licence says what you may now do, and only the second one is a permission.

patterns: what is the difference between pedagogy and teaching
entries.answer: Pedagogy is the theory and practice of teaching, and the word distinguishes the study of how learning happens from the craft of delivering a lesson, which is a distinction that matters once you are in front of a class. It covers the theories of what a learner is and how knowledge is built, the methods that follow from them, and the assessment that checks whether any of it happened. The main traditions disagree in a useful way: one treats the learner as receiving knowledge and the teacher as delivering it, one treats the learner as actively constructing understanding and the teacher as arranging conditions for it, and one treats the subject itself as what the learner must encounter before making sense of it. That last position is the reason a teacher sometimes has to insist on a formula before allowing a student to explore, which looks unhelpful and is usually deliberate. The practical version of all this is knowing when a class has stopped understanding, and the honest limit is that a teacher cannot see that directly and has to infer it from what students do.
